title: Your pencils
hint: Four pencils, chosen by value, plus a white eraser.
say: Four pencils today, chosen by value: two-H and H-B for your brightest areas, two-B for the mid-tones, and six-B for your very darkest darks. We'll use all four, one at a time. You'll also want a white eraser -- or an eraser pencil if you have one -- for lifting sharp highlights later on.

title: A tissue for blending
say: You'll also reach for a small tissue later on, to blend your shading smooth. We'll get there in a few steps — for now, just know it's coming.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip — that's what gives foil its soft, believable shine.

title: Where your balloon will sit
say: Before the first line — leave space around your balloon. It sits slightly off-centre, a little tilted, so check the size before any detail. Lightly mark where your balloon will sit. I'll wait.

title: Find the tilt before the outline
watchSay: Notice the tilt here — these first lines aren't straight up and down. They lean, just slightly, crossing near the middle.
say: Now your turn — lightly cross two tilted guide lines near your centre mark. Take your time. I'll wait.

card.title: Find the tilt before the outline
card.sub: Compare the guide lines before adding detail.

title: Block in the whole shape first
watchSay: Keep going all the way around — block in the whole star before fixing any single point. Size first, detail later.
say: Rough in all six points lightly, all the way around. Don't worry about perfect symmetry yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Block in the whole shape first
card.sub: Size and placement matter before any detail.

title: Turn corners into soft curves
watchSay: Notice the edges keep adjusting here — drawn, checked, and redrawn until the shape feels right. Even a careful hand corrects its lines. That's how a good shape is found.
say: Your turn. Soften each corner into a gentle curve. If a line looks wrong, just adjust it — that's normal, even in a careful drawing. I'll wait.

card.title: Turn corners into soft curves
card.sub: Foil has volume: let the edges bend.

title: Clean up with a light touch
watchSay: This pass keeps refining — a light touch, going back over a line that still needs adjusting before it's final.
say: Keep refining your own lines too, with a light touch. Nothing needs to be perfect yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Clean up with a light touch
card.sub: A light touch while the shape still settles.

title: Erasing the guide lines
watchSay: Now the guide lines get erased. They helped find the tilt and the shape at the start -- the outline is set now, so they're not needed anymore.
say: Gently erase your guide lines too, and keep your outline. Take your time.

card.title: Erasing the guide lines
card.sub: The tilt lines did their job — now let them go.

title: Separate the seam from the outline
watchSay: Look closely at the rim just inside the outline — that seam is separate from the outer edge, and it matters.
say: Add a thin line just inside your outline, like a seam. Keep that narrow gap visible. I'll wait.

card.title: Separate the seam from the outline
card.sub: Look for the narrow rim inside the edge.

title: Let folds turn toward the centre
watchSay: These small curves are folds in the foil. Notice how they turn from the rim toward the centre, not straight across.
say: Add a few light fold lines, curving in toward the middle. Just a few is enough. I'll wait.

card.title: Let folds turn toward the centre
card.sub: Follow each fold's direction.

title: Your outline is ready
watchSay: A few more fold marks, and the outline is complete — a strong shape with soft edges, ready for shading.
say: Take one more look at your whole outline before we bring in the light and dark. I'll wait.

card.title: Strong shape, soft edges
card.sub: Ready for light and dark.

title: Outline complete
hint: Your outline is ready — good place to pause.
say: Your outline is ready. That's the hardest part done. Good place to pause here if you'd like — next time, we bring in the light and dark.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Look closely at the edge
watchSay: In the outline, straight lines helped find the big shape fast. Now it's time to slow down and look closely at the edge. Still life is all about detail — every bump and dent in the foil is worth seeing.
say: Look at the reference. Find one edge that isn't straight. Take your time.

card.title: Look closely at the edge
card.sub: A straight guess, next to what's really there.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Move point to point
watchSay: Here, the outer edge gets followed one point at a time. Where the foil bulges, the line bulges. Where it dents, the line dips in. Once it matches what's really there, it gets darker.
say: Pick one point. Follow its edge slowly — look, then draw the bumps you see. Darken it only once you're sure.

card.title: Move point to point
card.sub: One point at a time, all the way around.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Light side, shadow side
watchSay: The light here comes from the upper left, so each point has a light side and a shadow side. Once an edge is confirmed, it's mostly the shadow side that gets darker.
say: Find your own light direction, then look closely at each edge before you darken it — mostly on the shadow side. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Light side, shadow side
card.sub: Light from the upper left — confirmed edges darken on the shadow side.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: A quick clean-up, then keep going
watchSay: Here, a line that didn't match gets lightened, then checked again. Observing means checking and correcting.
say: If an edge doesn't match what you see, lighten it and look again. There's no rush.

card.title: A quick clean-up, then keep going
card.sub: Check against what you see, then correct.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Leave the paper white here
watchSay: Notice what's happening inside each point — nothing, not yet. Right now only the edge is being refined. That white paper stays white, and later it becomes the bright shine of the foil.
say: Keep the inside of each shape empty for now — just refine the edge. Leave the paper white there. I'll wait.

card.title: Leave the paper white here
card.sub: Only the edge is being refined — this stays white.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Take a breath and compare
watchSay: Hands come off the page for a moment — this is a comparison against the real foil edge. Checking is part of observing, not just the drawing itself.
say: Hold your drawing at arm's length and compare it with the reference. Are any edges still too smooth or too straight? Foil edges wave.

card.title: Take a breath and compare
card.sub: Check your edges against the reference.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Edges confirmed
watchSay: A few more edges checked and confirmed, and the whole outline now matches what's really there — ready for tone.
say: Take one more look at your whole star — every edge checked against what you see. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Every edge checked against reality
card.sub: Ready for tone.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Light and dark complete
hint: Your edges now match what you really see — good place to pause.
say: Your edges now follow what you really see. That's real observation. Good place to pause here if you'd like — next, we build the tone across the whole form.

title: Stroke direction follows the form
watchSay: Watch the direction of these strokes — they follow the curve of each puffed section, not a flat grid. Tone that follows the form is what makes it look round, not flat.
say: Choose one section of your own star. Stroke in the direction that section curves, not straight up and down. Take your time.

card.title: Stroke direction follows the form
card.sub: Strokes run with the curve, not against it.

title: Keep following each curve
watchSay: Same idea, a new section — the stroke direction changes because the curve changes.
say: Move to another section. Let your strokes follow that section's own curve. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Keep following each curve
card.sub: A different section, a different direction.

title: Build it gradually
watchSay: Notice the tone builds in thin layers, not one heavy pass — the same area gets gone over more than once, always following the same curve.
say: Build your own tone the same way: light layers, more than one pass, rather than pressing hard once. Take it slowly.

card.title: Build it gradually
card.sub: Thin layers, more than one pass.

title: Another section, same patience
watchSay: Now another section gets the same gradual build-up, strokes still following its curve.
say: Pick another section and keep layering lightly, following its curve. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Another section, same patience
card.sub: Still light layers, still following the curve.

title: Still the same pencil
watchSay: Still the same HB — the deeper tone comes from more layers, not a softer pencil.
say: Keep building with your own HB. Add another layer wherever it still looks too light. I'll wait.

card.title: Still the same pencil
card.sub: More layers, not a softer pencil.

title: Keep the whole star moving together
watchSay: No single point gets finished before the next one starts — tone builds across the whole star together.
say: Don't chase one perfect section — add a little tone to several areas, then come back. Take your time.

card.title: Keep the whole star moving together
card.sub: A little tone everywhere, not one point finished.

title: Protect each highlight
watchSay: Look closely — it's not just one bright spot. Each puffed section keeps its own highlight, left white while the tone around it deepens.
say: Find each section's own brightest spot and leave it alone, even as you darken what's around it. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Protect each highlight
card.sub: Every section keeps its own bright spot.

title: Deepen the darks near each highlight
watchSay: Right next to each protected highlight, the tone jumps noticeably darker — the dark sits right next to the light, patch by patch, not a smooth fade. That's real contrast already; the darkest, crispest accents still come later, with a 6B pencil.
say: Push the tone darker right beside your own protected highlights. The bigger the jump, the brighter they'll read. There's no rush.

card.title: Deepen the darks near each highlight
card.sub: Dark next to light, patch by patch.

title: Last layers across the form
watchSay: A final round across the whole star — connecting the tones and filling any area that's still too pale. The contrast stays.
say: Take one more pass. Fill the areas that still look thin, but keep your highlights white and your darks strong.

card.title: Last layers across the form
card.sub: Connect the tones — keep the contrast.

title: Ready for the tissue
watchSay: Tone is built across the whole form now, with each highlight protected — next, a tissue will blend it smooth.
say: Take one more look at your whole star before we blend it smooth. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Every highlight protected
card.sub: Ready for the tissue.

title: Tone complete
hint: Tone is built across the whole form — good place to pause.
say: Tone is built across the whole star, with every highlight protected. That's real patience. Good place to pause here if you'd like — next, we blend it smooth with a tissue.

title: A clean corner, light pressure
watchSay: The tissue gets folded to a clean corner, then blended along the form — never in circles — with a light touch.
say: Fold your tissue to a clean corner and blend one area along the form. Light pressure. Take your time.

card.title: A clean corner, light pressure
card.sub: Blend along the form, not in circles.

title: Keep the highlight clean
watchSay: Close to the highlight — but never across it. Then the next area.
say: Blend each area the same way, right up to the highlight, never over it. Do the whole star. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Keep the highlight clean
card.sub: Every highlight stays protected, area by area.

title: Before and after
watchSay: Softer — but the contrast is still there. Smooth, not flat.
say: Compare your drawing with before. If a highlight turned grey, press a kneaded eraser on it gently to lift it back. Tap Continue when you're ready.

title: Blending complete
hint: Tone is smooth, contrast still there — good place to pause.
say: Your tone is smooth, and the contrast is still there. That's the balance foil needs. Good place to pause here if you'd like — next, we add the darkest details.

title: Folds set the rhythm
watchSay: Folds sit roughly parallel to each other, with some long and some short. That variety gives them rhythm. They are not all the same. Every fold follows the direction of the balloon's surface. Where the surface curves, draw the fold as a curve. Where it runs straight down, draw it straight. Observe first, then draw.
say: Pick up your 6B and look at your own star's folds first. Which are long, which are short? Which curve, which run straight? Observe, then draw just one or two.

card.title: Folds set the rhythm
card.sub: Long and short, curved and straight.

title: A fold between two points deepens
watchSay: Between the top point and the upper-right point, the surface folds inward -- the pencil presses hardest right there, in the crease itself, not on the flat panel beside it.
say: Choose one fold on your own star and press hardest only in the crease. Let the panel on either side stay lighter.

card.title: A fold between two points deepens
card.sub: Press hardest right in the crease.

title: Lifting a crisp highlight
watchSay: Here, a white block eraser comes in. Pressed corner-first right beside the fold just drawn, it lifts a thin, bright highlight -- dark fold, bright edge, side by side. Draw, then lift, and watch the fold get squeezed out by the light.
say: Use a sharp edge -- the corner of a white eraser, an eraser pencil, or a kneaded eraser pinched to a point -- to lift a thin highlight right beside the fold.

card.title: Lifting a crisp highlight
card.sub: Dark fold, bright edge, side by side.

title: Fold, then lift -- again
watchSay: On the left point, the same rhythm repeats -- fold drawn dark, then a thin highlight lifted right beside it. Fold, lift, fold, lift. Watch the texture of the foil start to appear.
say: Try the same pair on your own left point: darken the fold, then lift a highlight beside it. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Fold, then lift -- again
card.sub: The same rhythm, a different point.

title: The left point's edge gets dense new hatching
watchSay: New hatch marks build up fast along the left point's edge -- so much pressure that the pencil wears down to a stub and needs sharpening again before the next pass.
say: Add a few hatch strokes of your own along one edge. If your pencil goes dull, stop and sharpen it -- a sharp point keeps the dark crisp.

card.title: The left point's edge gets dense new hatching
card.sub: So much pressure the pencil wears down.

title: A clear look before going further
watchSay: Hands lift for just a moment -- a chance to check the whole star at arm's length. Is the dark staying concentrated in the folds, or spreading everywhere?
say: Hold your own drawing at arm's length. If the dark is spreading past the folds, that's worth noticing now, before adding more.

card.title: A clear look before going further
card.sub: Checking the dark against the light.

title: Freshly sharpened, back to the bottom point
watchSay: Pencil freshly sharpened, attention moves to the bottom point, right where it meets the stick, for the same dark-fold pass there.
say: Move to your own bottom point and begin the same pass -- dark in the fold, light protected beside it.

card.title: Freshly sharpened, back to the bottom point
card.sub: Right where the point meets the stick.

title: The stick gets its dark pass
watchSay: The stick gets its own dark pass with the pencil -- more than one layer, since it's one of the darkest parts of the whole drawing.
say: Give your own stick a few layers too. It can go darker than almost anywhere else on the page.

card.title: The stick gets its dark pass
card.sub: One of the darkest parts of the page.

title: The seam beside the stick turns crisp
watchSay: The same white block eraser reappears here, lifting a highlight right at the seam beside the stick -- then the pencil crosshatches around it, pass after pass, until the edge turns crisp.
say: Try the same combination again: lift a highlight with your eraser's edge, then crosshatch around it until the line feels crisp.

card.title: The seam beside the stick turns crisp
card.sub: The same eraser, lifting the edge sharp.

title: A pause to check the contrast
watchSay: The pencil lifts off the page for a moment, hovering right over the crosshatching just finished -- one more check that the dark-to-light jump is still strong.
say: Pause here too. Look at what you just darkened -- is the contrast beside it still crisp?

card.title: A pause to check the contrast
card.sub: Still sharp, still dark enough?

title: Back on the bottom point
watchSay: Work continues on the bottom point, deepening what's already dark rather than spreading new tone thin across the page.
say: Keep deepening darks you've already started, rather than opening up new areas everywhere.

card.title: Back on the bottom point
card.sub: Deepening, not spreading thin.

title: A last touch of tissue
watchSay: A tissue comes back out, just for a moment, to soften one facet near the lower-right point -- but even now, it stops right at the edge of the dark, never smoothing into it.
say: If an area feels too sharp-edged all over, a very light tissue touch can help -- but keep it away from your darkest accents.

card.title: A last touch of tissue
card.sub: Stopping right at the edge of the dark.

title: Knowing when to stop
watchSay: Only a few small touches now. Knowing when to stop is a skill too -- overworking makes the foil look dull and muddy.
say: Look for one or two places that still need it. If nothing does, you're done.

card.title: Knowing when to stop
card.sub: A skill, not a shortcut.

title: Compare with the finished reference
watchSay: Hands fully clear now -- here's the finished drawing: folds dark, highlights crisp, foil complete.
say: Put your drawing beside the finished reference. Where does yours shine? Pick one thing you're proud of.

title: Details complete
hint: Every fold is dark, every highlight crisp — the foil is complete.
say: Every fold is dark, every highlight crisp. That strong contrast is what makes foil look like foil. You've finished the drawing.

title: Look how far you've come
say: Five stages, one drawing: outline, observed edges, tone, blend, and now, details. Look how far you've come.

title: Share your drawing
hint: Outline · Observed edges · Tone · Blend · Details
say: Ready to share your finished balloon? Choose a clear photo, then tap send. You can also continue without one and come back later.
